title: Checks for some thread-unsafe functions against a black list of known-to-be-unsafe functions.
summary: Usually they access static variables without synchronization (e.g. gmtime(3)) or utilize signals in a racy way. The set of functions to check is specified with the FunctionSet option. The check is in the concurrency module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds pthread_setcanceltype function calls where a thread's cancellation type is set to asynchronous.
summary: Asynchronous cancellation type (PTHREAD_CANCEL_ASYNCHRONOUS) is generally unsafe, use type PTHREAD_CANCEL_DEFERRED instead which is the default. Even with deferred cancellation, a cancellation point in an asynchronous signal handler may still be acted upon and the effect is as if it was an asynchronous cancellation. The check is in the concurrency module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds undefined behavior caused by the bitwise left- and right-shift operator operating on integer types.
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.BitwiseShift. It applies to C, C++.

title: Check for logical errors for function calls and Objective-C message expressions (e.g., uninitialized arguments, null function pointers).
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.CallAndMessage. It applies to C, C++, Objective-C.

title: Check for division by zero.
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.DivideZero. It applies to C, C++, Objective-C.

title: Check for null pointers passed as arguments to a function whose arguments are references or marked with the 'nonnull' attribute.
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.NonNullParamChecker. It applies to C, C++, Objective-C.

title: Check for dereferences of null pointers.
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.NullDereference. It applies to C, C++, Objective-C.

title: Check for undefined arithmetic operations with null pointers.
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.NullPointerArithm. It applies to C, C++.

title: Check if the element count in new[] is garbage or undefined.
summary: clang-tidy runs it as the check clang-analyzer-core.uninitialized.NewArraySize. It applies to C++.
